skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Opinionated backend development standards for Node.js + Express + TypeScript microservices. Covers layered architecture, BaseController pattern, dependency injection, Prisma repositories, Zod validation, unifiedConfig, Sentry error tracking, async safety, and testing discipline.
skill.summary: Guides agents to build layered Node.js, Express, and TypeScript services with validation, observability, configuration, and tests.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown documentation, TypeScript examples, placeholder configuration, and anti-pattern examples. No prompt injection, malicious network activity, credential exfiltration, arbitrary file access, or command execution intent was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Example configuration values resemble secrets and can trigger scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label placeholders clearly and prefer obviously invalid sample values in documentation.

remediation.issue: Markdown backticks and relative imports create high static-analysis noise.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples as documentation, and add scanner suppressions or explanatory comments if the marketplace supports them.

content.value_statement: Backend services often drift into inconsistent routes, weak validation, and scattered configuration. This skill applies structured Node.js and Express standards for maintainable TypeScript microservices.
actual_capabilities: Applies layered route, controller, service, repository, and database boundaries.
Guides BaseController usage for consistent responses and error handling.
Recommends Zod schemas for request bodies, query parameters, and route parameters.
Promotes centralized unifiedConfig access instead of scattered environment reads.
Defines Prisma repository patterns, dependency injection, and transaction handling.
Adds expectations for Sentry observability, async safety, and focused backend tests.
limitations: It is a standards guide, not a runnable framework or code generator.
Examples assume Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, and Sentry.
It does not replace project-specific architecture review or threat modeling.
Some recommendations may need adaptation for non-Express backends.

use_cases.title: Design a New Service Endpoint
use_cases.description: Create a route, controller, service, repository, validation, and tests that follow the same backend structure.

use_cases.title: Review a Backend Pull Request
use_cases.description: Check whether changes preserve layer boundaries, use unified configuration, validate input, and capture errors.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Express Code
use_cases.description: Move business logic out of routes and into testable services with repositories and explicit error boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for adding a simple resource endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-dev-guidelines skill to design a simple Express endpoint for [resource]. Include route, controller, service, validation, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review Backend Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for checking an existing change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend change with the backend-dev-guidelines skill. Identify layer violations, missing validation, config issues, and test gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Route Logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for moving logic out of Express routes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this Express route using the backend-dev-guidelines skill. Move business logic into services and repositories, then describe required tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Backend Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for a higher-risk service modification.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the backend-dev-guidelines skill to plan this production backend change. Include feasibility risk, architecture impact, validation, observability, and rollout tests.

output_examples.input: Add a user creation endpoint to an Express service.
output: A route delegates directly to a controller without business logic.
The controller validates input, calls a service, and uses shared response helpers.
The service applies business rules and calls a repository method.
Unit and integration tests cover success, validation failure, and duplicate user behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a backend change that reads configuration in multiple files.
output: The review flags scattered configuration access as a maintainability risk.
The suggested fix moves values into unified configuration with startup validation.
The response lists tests for default values, missing secrets, and environment overrides.

output_examples.input: Refactor a route with database queries and error handling inline.
output: The route becomes a thin registration layer.
Database access moves behind a repository with intent-based methods.
Errors flow through the base controller and monitoring is added to critical paths.

best_practices: Use the skill before changing routes, controllers, services, repositories, middleware, or backend configuration.
Pair its architectural guidance with project-specific tests, security controls, and deployment requirements.
Ask for explicit tradeoffs when a recommendation conflicts with existing service patterns.
anti_patterns: Using the skill to bypass local code review, security review, or production readiness checks.
Applying its Express-specific patterns unchanged to unrelated backend frameworks.
Copying examples without replacing placeholders, secrets, routes, and service names for the target project.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps structure Node.js, Express, and TypeScript backend services with clear layers, validation, configuration, monitoring, and tests.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete backend application?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation and review, but the agent still works inside your existing project.

faq.question: Which tools and libraries does it assume?
faq.answer: It assumes Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Zod, unified configuration, Sentry, and common Node.js testing tools.

faq.question: Can it review legacy route handlers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify business logic in routes and suggest controller, service, and repository boundaries.

faq.question: Does it handle security requirements?
faq.answer: It promotes validation, centralized secrets access, and error handling, but it does not replace a full security review.

faq.question: Can teams adapt the rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should keep the core layer boundaries while adapting names, dependencies, and tests to local standards.
